data.gender_notes: Sadhana is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A person who seeks to attain a goal or an aim through self-discipline, meditation, and hard work. The name Sadhana represents the pursuit of knowledge, wisdom, and self-realization. The name Sadhana carries the meaning “Aim, Goal, Purpose” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sadhana usually hope their child will grow to embody aim, goal, purpose and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Sadhana represents the journey towards self-realization and enlightenment through spiritual practices and disciplines.
data.etymology: Sadhana belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Aim, Goal, Purpose.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sadhana total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Sadhana" holds great significance in Hindu culture and denotes the path towards spiritual growth. It represents dedication, discipline, and continuous effort put towards achieving a noble goal, be it worldly or spiritual. Sadhana practices, such as yoga, meditation, studying sacred texts, and performing rituals, have been an integral part of Hindu spiritual tradition for centuries and are still widely practiced today.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu philosophy, Sadhana symbolizes the journey towards self-realization and enlightenment. It is believed that through Sadhana, one can purify the mind, overcome inner obstacles, and connect with the divine. The name Sadhana holds a deep spiritual significance as it serves as a reminder of the inherent potential for growth and transformation within each individual. Through Sadhana, one can cultivate inner peace, deepen their understanding of the universe, and ultimately, attain freedom from the cycles of birth and death.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sadhana represents the dedicated spiritual practice and disciplined path towards achieving self-realization and union with the divine. It embodies the persistent effort to purify the mind and transform oneself through devotion, meditation, and righteous action.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'सद्धन' (sadhana), which means 'truth' or 'wealth'. In Hinduism, Sadhana refers to the spiritual practices or disciplines undertaken to attain self-realization or union with the divine.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sadhana was a renowned Hindu philosopher and scholar in the 12th century. The name Sadhana carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Sadhana was a prominent figure in Hindu philosophy and scholarship during the medieval period.
